overview.text: Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH) invites online bids for ERP and Web-based ERP-like solutions.
The RFP is structured into Volume I (Bidding Instructions) and Volume II (Technical Requirements).
This document is Volume I of the Request for Proposal.
IIT Hyderabad is a fully funded Autonomous Body under the Government of India established under the IITs Act 1961.
As of April 2020, the Institute has 220 faculty members and plans to accommodate over 4500 students by 2022.
The purpose is to implement an End-to-End Web-based ERP Solution for Academic and Administrative functions.
Tender documents can be downloaded from the e-tender portal, CPP Portal, or the IITH website.

scope.text: The solution should automate Academic and Administrative functions including Finance & Accounts, Stores & Purchases, Asset Management, HRM & Payroll, Estate Management, Project Management, and Asset Maintenance.
The proposed ERP solution should facilitate the smooth creation of new departments/centers/courses.
The system must enable smooth functioning, integration, and coordination of all units within the institute.
Bidders must either port data from existing systems or integrate them to the ERP system to be deployed.

important_dates.text: Bid Submission Close Date is 15 Mar 2021 at 1700 hrs
Opening of Technical Bids (Envelope 'A') is scheduled for 16 Mar 2021 at 1100 hrs

commercial_requirements.text: Bidder has to select the payment option as e-payment to pay the tender fee / EMD as applicable and enter details of the instrument.

In case of Bank Guarantee (BG), the BG in original should be posted/couriered/given in person to the concerned official of IIT Hyd before the Online Opening of Technical Bid. In case of non-receipt of BG in original by the said time, the uploaded bid will be summarily rejected.
Bidders are requested to note that they should necessarily submit their financial bids in the format provided and no other format is acceptable.

Bidder(s) must be registered with Tax Department (Self-Attested copy of the GST number issued by Government of India).
Bids not fulfilling the pre-qualification conditions given below will be rejected.

overview.text: Issuing organization is the Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IIT Hyderabad), located in Kandi, Sangareddy - 502 285, Telangana, India.
The RFP process involves a composite Quality Cum Cost Based Selection (QCBS) with 70% weightage for technical evaluation and 30% for commercial evaluation.
Technical bids are opened on the scheduled date, while price bids are opened on a later date to be announced subsequently.

scope.text: The scope of work covers implementing a web-based ERP system for Higher Education Institutes.
Implementation must adhere to Functional and Technical Requirement Specifications including Project Timelines and Payment Milestones.
Scope includes providing Post Implementation Application Maintenance and Enhancement Service (AMES) support.

important_dates.text: Price Bids of eligible bidders will be opened on a later date. The date and time for opening of the Price Bids will be announced later.

Quoted prices should be inclusive of charges for all activities in scope of work, all types of required support, licenses, upgrades, accessories, tools, utilities, patches required for full functionality of the proposed system.

overview.text: IITH is requesting a web-based ERP system implementation for technical evaluation.
The winning bid (H1) will be awarded based on the highest total score calculated with 70% technical and 30% commercial weightage.
IITH reserves the right to ask bidders for clarification, site visits, and presentations of their proposed ERP solution.

scope.text: Technical evaluation includes a presentation covering Parts A to E and a demo of modules in Part F.
Part A covers Bidder's Profile including years of operation, annual revenue, and proposed team details.
Part B requires the Project Plan, Implementation Methodology, Risk Mitigation Strategies, and Training Plans.
Part C evaluates functional requirements via a mapping of direct fit, future releases, third-party offerings, and customizations.
Part D covers Non-Functional capabilities including Architecture, Security, API usage, Scalability, and Automation tools.
Part E requires Solution Case Studies from the higher education sector and references for data migration/issue management tools.
Part F consists of Proof of Concept (POC) demonstrations specifically in Finance, Payroll, Stores & Purchases, Academics, and Issue Management.

requirements.text: Bidders must submit a document titled 'Response-To-Part-A-of-Technical-Evaluation.PDF'.
Bidders must submit a document titled 'Response-To-Part-B-of-Technical-Evaluation.PDF'.
Functional mapping must be submitted as a spreadsheet with mandatory fields including Module, Sub-module, Fitment Option, and supporting documents.
Detailed supporting documents like datasheets, user manuals, screenshots, integration methodology, and difficulty levels are required for customizations.
Part D response must include a document titled 'Response-To-Part-D-of-Technical-Evaluation.PDF'.
Part E requires client reference checks and case studies submitted following the format in Annexure V.
Bidders must provide reference checks for data migration and issue management tools used during the project tenure.
Only bidders scoring a minimum of 60% in Parts A to E are invited for Part F POC demonstrations.
Bidder responsibility for functional mapping includes defining fitment options with five specific categories: Direct Fit, Future Release, Third Party, Customization, or No Solution.

eligibility.text: Part A evaluation attributes include Years of Experience in the educational ERP domain and Annual Revenue over the past 5 years.
Table 1.3 specifies that Part A has a minimum of 6 marks required out of a maximum of 10 to meet technical eligibility thresholds.

important_dates.text: IITH may ask the Bidder for clarification regarding its bid, with replies received as part of the bid document.

important_conditions.text: Technical Bids must comply strictly to all Specifications, Scope of Work, Eligibility Criteria, and Terms & Conditions without deviations, exceptions, objections, conditionality or reservations.
IITH may require clarifications; no change in Price of the bid shall be sought, offered or permitted via clarification.
Bidder must submit a presentation of the proposed ERP solution and arrange site visits to similar client implementations as requested.
Technically Acceptable bids (complying with Parts A-E) shall undergo Price bid evaluation before declaration as Technically Acceptable.
Technical evaluation consists of 6 Parts (A-F), carrying 70% overall weightage, split across 600 marks minimum (140 required for A-E combined).
To be invited for POC demonstration in Part F, the bidder must achieve a minimum of 60% score for each of Parts A to E.
Any variation found during evaluation/demonstration deemed fraudulent is liable for forfeiture of the PBG without prejudice to other legal remedies.

overview.text: The RFP is issued by the Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad (IITH), located at Kandi, Sangareddy - 502 285, Telangana, India.

scope.text: Part A evaluates Bidder Credentials, years of experience in the educational ERP domain, Annual Revenue, Project Management Capabilities, and proposed Support Team.

Part B covers Implementation Approach & Methodology including Project Plan, Business Design, Risks & Mitigation Strategies, Detailed timelines, Training, Change Management, Documentation, and Escalation Matrix.
Part C assesses Functional Evaluation as per FRSs through Standard ERP Solution, Future ERP Releases, Third Party offerings, or Customizations.
Part D covers Non-Functional (Technical) Capabilities such as Architecture, Modularity, Scalability, Security Framework, API usage, and backup/restore mechanisms.
Part E requires Solution Case Studies & Client References, specifically focusing on client base in the higher education sector in India (especially other IITs).
Part F requires Proof of Concept Demonstration for Finance and Accounting, Payroll, Stores & Purchases, Academics, and Issue Management System modules.

scope.text: The project scope includes development and delivery of Core Modules and Other Modules with an Architecture and Design phase completing within 4 months.
Payment milestones include a 15% release upon completion of detailed Architecture and Design for both core and other modules.
A further 10% payment is released upon successful delivery of Conference Room Pilot (CRP) demos, within 12 months for Core and 15 months for Other Modules.
Payments proceed upon successful cross-functional integration, load/stress testing, beta release, and Go-Live at the institute level, requiring completion within 15-18 months.
A 30% (Core) / 40% (Other) payment is released after end-to-end beta testing and commissioning of the stable version with User Acceptance Test (UAT) approval at 24 months.
Final payments for Core Modules occur after a 12-month warranty period, while Other Modules require completion within 24 months.
Core Modules must be completed within 15 months from the date of agreement signing, and Other Modules within 18 months.
Additional payments are required for data migration from legacy systems and integration with legacy systems upon successful production deployment.
The scope includes Application Maintenance & Enhancement Services (AMES) Support provided as equal quarterly instalments for three years post-warranty.

important_dates.text: Preference will be given to Make in India products while evaluating bids.

The Warranty period is 12 months and it starts after 24 Months.
